title: Interpretable Active Learning for Pedigree Data Deduplication in Cancer Genetics.
authors: Rosito, Maria S; Cervantes, Aleck E; Hong, Christine; Bonner, Joseph D; Nehoray, Bita; Schwartz Levine, Alison; Rosenberg, Danna; Anez-Bruzual, Isabel; Parmigiani, Giovanni; Amos, Christopher I; Garber, Judy E; Gruber, Stephen B; Braun, Danielle
one_liner_zh: 该文研究癌症遗传学中家系数据去重的可解释主动学习方法，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或分子模拟，与本课题无关。
abstract: PURPOSE: Studying rare genetic conditions often requires multicenter research to gather sufficient data. However, data from multiple institutions may include relatives from the same family enrolled at different sites, increasing the likelihood of duplicate records. This issue is compounded by the use of deidentified data, which limits the direct linkage through personal identifiers. These redundancies can bias family-based genetic studies underscoring the need for robust methods for pedigree deduplication. We propose an interpretable, active learning-based approach to efficiently identify duplicate records in genetic studies, with specific application to families with TP53 mutations in the Li-Fraumeni and TP53: Understanding and Progress (LiFT UP) study. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Our approach combines heuristic labeling with graph-based features and a machine learning model to iteratively refine duplicate detection. We first generate a partially labeled data set leveraging mutation variant diversity and family characteristics. A random forest classifier is then trained to predict duplicate pairs, with active learning guiding iterative refinement. This method is applied to real-world pedigree data from the LiFT UP study to assess its effectiveness in a multicenter setting. RESULTS: Our method labeled pedigree pairs in data from the LiFT UP study with a high degree of automation, achieving 99.95% automated processing in the deduplication workflow. By prioritizing likely duplicates for human review, it minimized manual effort while aiming for high specificity. This automated approach avoids dependence on rule-based filters, such as identifier matching, which ultimately require manual confirmation, offering a more scalable solution for improving data quality in risk estimation. CONCLUSION: Interpretable active learning provides an effective solution for pedigree deduplication. Future work will explore refinements in identifying potential duplicates and evaluate its generalizability across other genetic data sets.
abstract_zh: 目的：研究罕见遗传疾病通常需要多中心研究以收集足够的数据。然而，来自多个机构的数据可能包括在不同地点登记的同一家族亲属，从而增加了重复记录的可能性。这一问题因使用去标识化数据而加剧，这限制了对个人标识符的直接关联。这些冗余可能使基于家族的遗传研究产生偏倚，凸显了对家系去重稳健方法的需求。我们提出一种可解释的、基于主动学习的方法，以高效识别遗传研究中的重复记录，并具体应用于Li-Fraumeni和TP53：理解与进展（LiFT UP）研究中携带TP53突变的家族。材料与方法：我们的方法结合了启发式标记、基于图的特征和机器学习模型，以迭代优化重复检测。我们首先生成一个部分标记的数据集，利用突变变异多样性和家族特征。然后训练一个随机森林分类器来预测重复对，并通过主动学习指导迭代优化。该方法应用于LiFT UP研究的真实家系数据，以评估其在多中心环境中的有效性。结果：我们的方法在LiFT UP研究数据中标记家系对时实现了高度自动化，在去重流程中达到99.95%的自动处理率。通过优先将可能的重复项提交人工审查，它在追求高特异性的同时最小化了人工努力。这种自动化方法避免了对基于规则的过滤器（如标识符匹配）的依赖，这些过滤器最终需要人工确认，从而为改善风险估计中的数据质量提供了更具可扩展性的解决方案。结论：可解释的主动学习为家系去重提供了有效解决方案。未来工作将探索识别潜在重复项的改进方法，并评估其在其他遗传数据集上的泛化能力。
